_about: Monta T-bar (surface lift, modern), rebuilt to the owner's reference installation: the drive at the bottom (D1) and the return at the top, a tower kit (heads, 1 m mast sections, base; every mast leaning across the line, D11), the carriers (recoil box on its grip, T bar and J bar) and the operator hut. Millimetres in the lift frame: origin on the bullwheel's axle (a terminal) or the mast top (a head) or at grade (a base, mast section, hut), u toward the line (uphill on a tower), v right, w up. The loaded (uphill) rope is on the right going up: v+ at the bottom terminal, v- at the top one.

common._sheave: v3 (R1, R2): 350 dished discs with a thin liner band (rim to dia, ~15 % of the radius)

train._about: A sheave train on one rope: sheaves in pairs on rockers (a cast web inboard, rockerThick, a thin cheek plate outboard, cheekThick), the rockers' pins on a pentagonal equaliser inboard of them, the equaliser on the end pin through the crossarm's end plate (a terminal's long row may hang its rockers in pairs on yokes, the main equaliser one plate further inboard). Support trains stand on the pin with the rope on top; hold-down trains hang inverted from the same pin. The axles sit on an arc of radius arcR about the rope's bend. Offsets in v run inboard from the sheave's hub: cheek gap, web, equaliser gap, equaliser, end gap, end plate.

tower._lean: D11/Q1: every mast leans this many degrees across the line toward the loaded track; ropes level, the foundation off to the return side

base._stub: the mast's first stretch is part of the base, wrapped in the red tower pad (D5, plain with a light cap ring at its top, R6); mast_foot at its top along the leaned axis

head._v3: R3 one tall cone from the sleeve to the flange; R4/R26 the platform (now the catwalk on the head, owner 2026-11-03); R7 triangular gussets; R27 curled hook brackets for the wire (now on the lifting beam); R29 smooth catchers, longer on the drag (+v) side; R32 octagonal pin covers the arm's depth
head._portal: the lifting frame (owner, 2026-11-03: a mini fixed-grip head): the Sessellift FGQ-4 tower's lifting portal (sessellift_fgq4.json drive.portal, crossbeam.footPlates) scaled by the gauge ratio 3000/4120, so its lifting eyes sit over the T-bar's ropes as the chair's sit over its own; centred on the head (u 0) and standing on the arm's top (w 320). Two legs leaning out from foot plates to a bolted lifting beam, lug plates with eyes at its ends, J-handrails; read by liftkit.heads.portal
head._numberPlate: as on the chair towers: a black plate stood off the lifting beam's face toward the bottom station (-u), where riders come from, scaled with the frame (the chair's 400 x 260 x 0.728); stood off past the kit's 15 mm bolt heads
head._catwalk: the catwalk on the head (owner, 2026-11-03: replaces the platform ring round the mast): the chair towers' head platform, drawn by the same liftkit.heads.entry_platform in its own format, beside the arm on the ladder's side (+u) with its deck level with the arm's top, at walking size (not scaled with the gauge): a grated deck 600 deep in two halves either side of the ladder hatch, the end member on the arm's face, a U hoop rail 1.06 m high with a mid rail across its outer edge, two struts back down to the arm's foot; 2.1 m wide (v), its ends 0.45 m inside the ropes as on the chair's line towers; the mast ladder climbs on through the hatch (centred on the leaned ladder where it meets the deck), grab rails 1 m above the deck
head._catcher: black tube out from each end of each train, inside the carrier hanger's D (out of v, below the rope), so a swinging hanger can't reach the sheaves: a smooth sweep outboard and down, the same on both ropes (owner, v3.1)

drive._about: The bottom station (D1): one box column on a concrete block, its lower part the cabinet, a slim side cabinet and gussets at its foot; a head frame of two girders along the line; the bullwheel hung under a hoop-railed grating deck behind the column (the deck ends over the wheel's centre, its back half in the open, R8) with the machinery house on it (louvres on its back end, windows on its -v side); toward the line a separate narrower platform a step down (trainDeck.drop) over two hold-down trains (8 sheaves on the leaving loaded rope, v+, 4 on the arriving one); the loading hoop just under the leaving train on a short rod from a bracket off its girder, outboard of the bars (R12). No braces, no ladder (R10, R11). Rope at 3.4 m (D8).
drive._hoop: the loading hoop (R12): a black ring in the u-w plane hanging just under the loaded train on a short rod from a bracket off its girder, outboard of the bars' path where the operator steadies them

return._about: The top station: one rectangular HSS diagonal leaning back toward the wheel, the main support (owner, v3.1), on a bolted base flange on the pad and bolted flanges under the head's cross girder (owner, v3.2), and a slim plumb box prop from the pad up to the diagonal's middle (owner, v3.1), carrying the girders bare (R16): a hoop-railed grating platform over the trains and another round the bearing beside the wheel, the box-section gallows for the wire between them (R17); the bullwheel cantilevered behind on its shaft from a bearing housing (the tensioning hidden inside, D2); toward the line an 8-sheave breakover row on each rope (owner, v3.1): support trains hung below the girders on drop plates, on the station arc, their rockers in pairs on two yokes under the main equaliser (yokeDrop; eqDrop from the rocker pins to the end pin), turned so the rope runs level from the wheel onto the first sheave and breaks over toward the line (restExit at rest; posable, the game re-poses them for the line's angle with the first sheave held); a thin guard rail round the wheel and along the rows, following the rope (R18); a galvanised ladder up the diagonal's line face to the trains' platform, whose railing opens at its head. Rope at 4.5 m at the wheel (Q4).
return._column: the diagonal (owner, v3.2): a rectangular HSS 508 x 305 (depth along the line face's normal, width across), corners rounded, its ends cut level; footU and topU where its axis meets the base flange and the head flanges
return._flanges: the diagonal's bolted connections (owner, v3.2): its base flange on the pad on anchor bolts, nuts on top; at its head its own flange bolted up under a matching flange on the cross girder (girderStep wider all round), nuts underneath; bolts in mm from the flange's centre, mirrored both ways
return._prop: the plumb prop (owner, v3.1): from a base plate on the pad up to the diagonal's wheel-side face at `at` of its length, a clevis of two plates and a pin there

hut._about: The operator hut (D9, Q3): red walls on skids, a mono-pitch white roof falling toward +u, the door and a window on the -u face, a window each side.

carrier._about: Carriers: a small dark clamp grip on the rope's outboard side; from it one hanger tube sweeps outboard and down in a half ellipse (the rope its straight side, a D) and comes back in to the recoil box, a pale rounded housing that hangs on a pin through its upper part, swinging fore and aft, nearly back under the rope; the cord leaves a collar at its bottom. The bar: a yellow stem with a plain socket at its top where the cord ends, and one continuous black padded crossbar (T) or a yellow J curve. Grip origin on the rope; u the way the carrier travels, +v outboard, w up. The bars' origin at their eye (the socket's top).

grip._grip: the clamp outboard of the sheaves' faces (vIn past the sheave's half width), its thin jaw reaching in to the rope inside the liners' clearance, so it passes support and hold-down sheaves and the bullwheel's groove (C12)

jBar._j: owner 2026-11-06: the T bar with one side cut off (no hooked tip): tBar's stem and pad to -v, stopping this far past the stem
